title: Daily X narrative digest — 2026-10-07

hits.name: levelsio
hits.text:
I own land and property in exactly these areas and will keep buying land and property in these areas

This is exactly my post-AGI thesis too

Scarse coastal or mountain land with clean air
hits.hook: I own land and property in exactly these areas and will keep buying land and property in these areas  This is exactly my
hits.quote_note: @IterIntellectus: post-ASI rich move to Mediterranean/coastal towns
hits.draft_en:
Pieter's post-AGI thesis: buy scarce coastal or mountain land with clean air. He already owns it and keeps buying.

When AI makes software and labor cheap, the scarce things are the ones you cannot copy. Land, trust, attention, taste.

You do not need property to apply it. Ask what in your work AI cannot copy, and spend more time on that.

Write down three things in your business that would still be scarce if code were free.
hits.video_tip: 10s: 'cost of code' ticker falling, then a coastline photo with a 'scarce' tag, caption own what AI can't copy.

hits.name: Alex Finn
hits.text: A lot of people don’t realize they’re 5 hours of vibe coding with Opus 5.5 away from changing their entire financial lives
hits.hook: A lot of people don’t realize they’re 5 hours of vibe coding with Opus 5.5 away from changing their entire financial liv
hits.draft_en:
"A lot of people don't realize they're 5 hours of vibe coding with Opus 5.5 away from changing their entire financial lives."

425k views for Alex Finn.

The line works because it is specific: one model, one number of hours, one big outcome.

The honest version: 5 hours gets you a working prototype. The money comes from the next 50 hours of selling it.

Spend your 5 hours this weekend. Then post the prototype and ask who would pay for it.
hits.video_tip: 10s: timer counting 5 hours over a code editor, then a second timer '50h selling' starts, caption build in 5, sell in 50.

hits.name: levelsio
hits.text:
Airbnb just responded to "reviewgate"

The replies here are literally hundreds of people who got their reviews removed directly contradicting what Airbnb says here

The "policy" they have seems to be to remove a guest's review and rating whenever a host asks for it

I don't get
hits.hook: Airbnb just responded to "reviewgate"  The replies here are literally hundreds of people who got their reviews removed d
hits.draft_en:
Airbnb answered "reviewgate" and the replies did the fact check.

Hundreds of people say their reviews were removed after a host asked. Pieter's read: short term, a 4.99 everywhere sells more nights. Long term, people learn the number means nothing and leave.

That trade shows up in every product with a score: app store ratings, AI eval dashboards, NPS.

If users can see the gap between your number and their experience, the number is now a liability.

Audit what gets removed from your reviews this week, and publish the rule.
hits.video_tip: 10s: official statement card, then a flood of reply bubbles saying 'mine got removed', caption the replies are the fact check.

hits.draft_en:
OpenAI opened its Decisions API in public beta, with image input.

Tony Dinh's whole reaction: They even support image input. RIP Jev.

154k views on a few words, because everyone knows the pattern. Every platform API launch kills a few wrapper startups the same afternoon.

If your product is one API call away from the model provider, your edge has to be workflow, data or distribution.

Write down what you would still have if your provider shipped your core feature tomorrow.
hits.video_tip: 8s: startup logo next to an API launch card, a tombstone slides in, caption what's left if they ship it.

hits.name: levelsio
hits.text:
Researchers have now found extremely high amounts of PFAS in the majority of Dutch tap water

The Netherlands was long known for having some of the cleanest tap water in the world and every Dutch person would drink from it, but that turned out to be false

It's full of PFAS!
hits.hook: Researchers have now found extremely high amounts of PFAS in the majority of Dutch tap water  The Netherlands was long k
hits.quote_note: own Sep 22 Dutch tap water post
hits.draft_en:
Dutch tap water was famous for being some of the cleanest in the world. New research says most of it has very high PFAS levels.

The reputation outlived the reality.

Tools do that too. A model, a library or a SaaS you trusted two years ago is still coasting on that trust.

Re-test the things you stopped checking: your stack, your vendors, your default model.

Pick one default you have not questioned in a year and benchmark it this week.
hits.video_tip: 8-10s: glass of water, a lab readout overlay climbs, caption re-test what you stopped checking.

hits.name: levelsio
hits.text:
Respect for @MistralAI for actually getting close now

It shows Europe can still do stuff if they just all get on the same page

hits.quote_note: Mistral Large 4 launch (community note: 38 is score not rank)
hits.draft_en:
Mistral Large 4 lands just behind DeepSeek, GLM and Kimi on the intelligence index, and ahead of every US open-weight model.

Pieter's read: Europe can still do stuff if it gets on the same page. A Community Note added that 38 is the index score, not the rank.

The bigger point holds. Open-weight models are now close enough to test on real work.

Run your most common prompt on Mistral Large 4 this week and compare it with your default model, side by side.
hits.video_tip: 10s: leaderboard bars sliding into place with a Mistral bar near the Chinese models, caption test the open model this week.

Greg Isenberg says there are only 13 categories of businesses left to build in the agentic era, and everything else is in decline.

110k views on a list plus a 25-minute breakdown.

Posts that say what is dying get shared, because nobody wants to be building the wrong thing.

Write your own version: three businesses agents make easier, three they make obsolete. One real example each. Post it.
hits.video_tip: 10s: grid of business icons, most fade to gray, a few glow, caption what's left to build.

hits.text:
Brazilians, what's the best washing machine, drier, fridge, freezer and AC brands? 

Because Brazil has import bans/taxes on everything so you can't easily get Euro brands like Miele, Bosch, etc.

For AC, I'd go with Mitsubishi or LG but not sure if available in BR?
hits.hook: Brazilians, what's the best washing machine, drier, fridge, freezer and AC brands?   Because Brazil has import bans/taxe
hits.draft_en:
Pieter asked Brazilians which washing machine, fridge, freezer and AC brands to buy, because import taxes block Miele and Bosch.

96k views. Almost 300 replies.

A real question to a named group beats a hot take for replies. People love being the expert for one minute.

Before you pick your next AI tool, ask your audience a specific question and name exactly who you want answers from.
hits.video_tip: 8s: question card 'Brazilians, which brand?' with reply bubbles stacking fast, caption ask a named crowd.

hits.name: levelsio
hits.text: Maybe it's working?
hits.hook: Maybe it's working?
hits.draft_en:
Three words: maybe it's working?

After a full day of posts about Airbnb reviews, Pieter's follow-up is a tiny progress check, and it climbs to about 95k.

Campaigns on X work when you report back. People who saw the first post want to know what happened.

If you call out a product in public, post the update when it moves, even if it is small.

Close the loop on your last callout today.
hits.video_tip: 8s: post timeline with a small 'update' bubble popping in, caption close the loop.

hits.name: Logan Kilpatrick
hits.text:
Nano Banana 2.1 is here! 

It’s a nice update for image generation and editing customers, comes with higher quality images, lots of bug fixes from previous models, and a new lower price point!

Available in the API, AI Studio, and Gemini app!
hits.hook: Nano Banana 2.1 is here!   It’s a nice update for image generation and editing customers, comes with higher quality imag
hits.draft_en:
Nano Banana 2.1 is out: higher quality images, bug fixes, and a lower price point. Live in the API, AI Studio and the Gemini app.

86k views for Logan's post.

The price drop is the quiet story. When image generation gets cheaper, every business selling AI visuals gets better margins overnight.

If you sell anything made with AI images, rerun your cost per asset this week and update your pricing.
hits.video_tip: 8s: image grid sharpening while a price tag ticks down, caption cheaper images, fatter margins.

hits.name: levelsio
hits.text:
There's a reason I've been porting so many classic games I liked to web with WASM and why this is taking off now I think

Because it's way easier to just open a new tab, type the URL and start playing than...

Switching on a console or gaming PC, waiting for it to boot,
hits.hook: There's a reason I've been porting so many classic games I liked to web with WASM and why this is taking off now I think
hits.quote_note: @tenobrus on free playable WASM versions of AAA games
hits.draft_en:
Pieter's theory on why free browser ports of classic games are taking off: opening a tab and typing a URL beats booting a console or a gaming PC.

Zero install wins.

AI tools work the same way. The demo that runs in a browser tab gets tried. The one that needs a download gets bookmarked and forgotten.

Cut the install step from your first-run experience. Ship a link that works in under 5 seconds.
hits.video_tip: 10s: console boot screen loading forever vs a browser tab launching a game instantly, caption zero install wins.

hits.name: Alex Finn
hits.text:
Hark is an awesome AI agent

Was lucky enough to have early access over the last week

Some things I really like about it:
• Best interface in agents. Period. Beautiful to look at and also completely customizable

• Extremely proactive. Constantly giving you ideas on what it
hits.hook: Hark is an awesome AI agent  Was lucky enough to have early access over the last week  Some things I really like about i
hits.draft_en:
Hark Pro launched. Alex Finn's first point was not the model. It was the interface: beautiful and fully customizable.

Second point: extremely proactive.

In a market where every agent looks like the same chat box, design is a moat again.

Screenshot your agent's main screen next to two competitors. If you cannot tell them apart, fix that before you add another feature.
hits.video_tip: 8s: three identical chat UIs side by side, one morphs into a custom interface, caption design is the moat.

hits.name: Alex Finn
hits.text:
This new AI agent blew my mind

Hark is a proactive agent with a custom interface that completely transforms based on who you are

They gave me early access a week ago and I've really enjoyed using it

Here's everything you need to know about Hark:
hits.hook: This new AI agent blew my mind  Hark is a proactive agent with a custom interface that completely transforms based on wh
hits.draft_en:
Alex Finn had a week of early access to Hark, a proactive agent whose interface changes based on who you are.

The pitch is not smarter answers. It is an agent that brings you ideas before you ask.

Proactive is the new bar. Chatbots wait for a prompt. The next wave shows up with a plan.

If you build an agent, add one thing it does without being asked, like a morning suggestion based on yesterday's work.
hits.video_tip: 10s: empty chat box vs an agent card popping up 'here's what to do today', caption proactive beats reactive.

hits.name: levelsio
hits.text:
There's very few logistics jobs now that won't be done way better by a self driving vehicle

The faster we replace humans in trucks with self driving vehicles, the less accidents and deaths we'll have
hits.hook: There's very few logistics jobs now that won't be done way better by a self driving vehicle  The faster we replace human
hits.quote_note: @Molson_Hart video of Amazon Freight driver hitting building
hits.draft_en:
An Amazon Freight truck hit a building. Pieter's take: very few logistics jobs will not be done better by self-driving vehicles, and faster replacement means fewer accidents and deaths.

Safety is becoming the main argument for automation, not cost.

If you build AI for physical work, lead with the risk you remove, not the headcount you cut.

Safety pitches get adopted. Layoff pitches get fought.

Rewrite your AI pitch so the first line is the harm it prevents.
hits.video_tip: 10s: crash news card fades into a self-driving dashboard with an accident counter at zero, caption sell the risk you remove.

TIL a crazy number of hotels is owned not by public stock holders, not by private owners, not even by private equity funds, but by governments!

You don't see this easily, because you have to dig quite deep (or well dig upward actually) and they cover it up in lots of
hits.hook: TIL a crazy number of hotels is owned not by public stock holders, not by private owners, not even by private equity fun
hits.quote_note: own Oct 5 post on hotel ownership filter
hits.draft_en:
TIL from Pieter: a crazy number of hotels are not owned by stockholders, private owners or even private equity. They are owned by governments.

You only see it if you dig up the ownership chain, which he did to build a new filter for his hotel site.

That is the content loop. Ship a data feature, then post the weirdest thing the data showed you.

Pull one surprising fact out of your own product data today and post it with the receipt.
hits.video_tip: 10s: ownership tree climbing up from a hotel to a government flag, caption ship the feature, post the surprise.

hits.name: levelsio
hits.text:
I agree with this

All AI companies should have 0% tax for next 10 years in EU

Instant boost to the mostly non-existing AI ecosystem in EU which will then suddenly start existing!
hits.hook: I agree with this  All AI companies should have 0% tax for next 10 years in EU  Instant boost to the mostly non-existing
hits.quote_note: @d4m1n: EU should cut all their taxes
hits.draft_en:
Pieter's fix for Europe's missing AI ecosystem: 0% tax for AI companies for the next 10 years.

Instant boost to an ecosystem that mostly does not exist yet, which would then suddenly start existing.

The take spreads because it is one number and one timeline. Policy posts go viral when they fit in a sentence.

If you have a view on how your country should win at AI, write it as one number and one deadline. Then post it.
hits.video_tip: 8s: EU map with a big '0% for 10 years' stamp, startup icons popping up, caption one number, one deadline.

hits.name: levelsio
hits.text: Anyone know how to enable Alexa+ in Portugal? Alexa regular never understands what we says. Alexa+ has an LLM behind it so should work better. It's not available in Portugal, but must be hackable?
hits.hook: Anyone know how to enable Alexa+ in Portugal? Alexa regular never understands what we says. Alexa+ has an LLM behind it
hits.draft_en:
Regular Alexa never understands Pieter. Alexa+ has an LLM behind it, but it is not available in Portugal.

His question: must be hackable?

There is a market in that sentence. Millions of people own devices that got smart in one country and stayed dumb everywhere else.

Geo-locked AI features are a gap indie builders can fill.

List one AI feature that is US-only. Build the version for everyone else.
hits.video_tip: 8s: smart speaker with a 'not available in your region' toast, then a wrench icon, caption build the unlocked version.

hits.draft_en:
There are guides and YouTube videos teaching Airbnb hosts how to get guest reviews removed.

Pick a reason: retaliation, extortion, irrelevant, private info, discrimination. The guides even rank the odds. Discrimination and extortion: very high.

If you run any moderation or review flow, search YouTube for how to beat it. Then close the top loophole.

Your users already watched the guide.

His point: almost everyone over 30 has belly fat. Hard to be lean at 40, let alone 49.

Builders who spend 12 hours a day next to an AI agent are the most at risk. The agent works while you wait.

So use the wait. Every long agent run, do one set of pushups or a 5-minute walk.

Count your agent-run workouts this week and post the number.

Real buildings around Praça do Comércio. Not exact, close enough to play with friends.

The new shortcut for games: real-world data plus a frontier model equals instant levels.

Pick your own city. Pull its OSM data and ask a model to turn one neighborhood into a playable map this weekend.
hits.video_tip: 12s: OSM street map morphs into a 3D shooter map, players run across the square, caption your city is a level now.

Pieter posted a US Secretary of State quote about Portugal and Greece being strong allies, and it pulled about 33k views.

He lives in Portugal and has spent weeks posting about countries competing for people. Any headline that touches that home turf gets his audience's attention.

When news lands on your niche, you are the obvious person to react.

Know your two or three home topics. When a headline hits one, post your angle within the hour.

Pieter put all of Quake III, with working multiplayer, inside a tweet. You click and play right in the feed.

A tweet used to be a link to your software. Now it can be the software.

If people can try your product without leaving the timeline, the trial step disappears. No signup, no tab, no install.

Find the smallest playable version of your app and make it run where your audience already scrolls.

Ask your audience one either/or question about their AI stack this week. Then post the results with your own pick and the reason.

Tobi shared Moritz Kremb's Claude-made video about being European. Dharmesh: this is so good, apologies to those who cannot watch it in their region.

A model made that video a day after one prompt, and founders are passing it around.

AI video is good enough now that the idea is the scarce part.

Write one prompt about the culture you know best and let a model make the video this week.

hits.name: Alex Finn
hits.text:
The Claude Bot everyone has been waiting for has arrived and it's.... Grok Bot

Elon announced Grok Bot will now be powered by whatever the BEST model is for the task you're working on

Ask for a super complex task? Opus 5.5

Ask for a detailed image? Midjourney

hits.hook: The Claude Bot everyone has been waiting for has arrived and it's.... Grok Bot  Elon announced Grok Bot will now be powe
hits.quote_note: @elonmusk on Grok Bot using best backend model per task
hits.draft_en:
Alex Finn says Elon announced Grok Bot will run on whatever model is best for the task you are working on. A complex task gets Opus 5.5. A detailed image gets Midjourney.

Routing beats loyalty. The assistant that picks the right model per job wins over one tied to a single lab.

Stop asking which model is best. Ask which model is best for each task.

Write that table for your own work today: task, model, why.
hits.video_tip: 10s: one assistant icon routing tasks to different model logos, caption the best model per task.

hits.name: Ben Tossell
hits.text:
i've gotten pretty comfy with my local tools and files and skills. 

now you're telling me cloud is better.

hits.hook: i've gotten pretty comfy with my local tools and files and skills.   now you're telling me cloud is better.   how do i d
hits.draft_en:
Ben Tossell got comfy with his local tools, files and skills. Now everyone says cloud agents are better. His question: how do I do that?

A lot of builders are stuck right here.

Local feels fast and private. Cloud agents run while you sleep and test your app for you.

You do not have to pick. Keep your skills and files in a repo, and let both local and cloud agents read it.

Move one skill folder into git today so any agent can use it.
hits.video_tip: 10s: laptop folder of skills sliding into a git repo, then local and cloud agents both pulling from it, caption one repo, every agent.

hits.draft_en:
Hassan launched GeoGuess Bench: 210 photos from around the world, every model guesses where each one was taken, scored by how close it gets.

Fun benchmarks travel further than serious ones. Everyone gets GeoGuessr. Few people read eval tables.

If you want to show which model is best for your use case, turn the test into a game anyone understands.

Build a 20-question benchmark for your niche and post the leaderboard.

hits.name: Ben Tossell

hits.hook: a lot has launched today
hits.draft_en:
Ben Tossell, five words: a lot has launched today.

Same day: Nano Banana 2.1, Hark Pro, OpenAI's Decisions API, GeoGuess Bench and Mistral Large 4 chatter.

Launch days are noise. The accounts that win them post a calm take on what actually matters.

Pick one launch from today, test it for 20 minutes, and post the one thing it changes for you.
hits.video_tip: 8s: launch cards flooding the screen, then all fade except one with a timer '20 min test', caption pick one, test it.

hits.name: Ben Tossell

hits.draft_en:
Ben Tossell: my dot/bot/muse/instinct decisions will die when pi bot is born.

Five personal agents in one sentence, and still no clear pick.

When a category is that crowded, users wait for the winner. Features stop mattering.

If you build a personal agent, the pitch is the one job you do that the others do not.

Write that job in one line and put it at the top of your landing page today.
hits.video_tip: 8s: five agent logos spinning on a wheel, one line of text stops it, caption one job beats five features.

Personal AI apps are the easy wins now: one user, one daily decision, real data.

Pick one decision you make every morning and build a tiny app that makes it for you this weekend.

virals.angle: The tools are almost free. Your time isn't.
virals.inspired_by: @claudeai Startups program (3.67M) + @rampatra_ (531k) + @AlexFinn 5 hours of vibe coding (425k)
virals.draft_en:
Anthropic just expanded Claude Startups: a year of Claude Team, API credits and office hours with their Applied AI team.

One indie founder posted that he got about €550 a month of Claude Code. Five Pro accounts, free, for a year.

Same day, Alex Finn's line pulled 425k views: you are 5 hours of vibe coding away from changing your financial life.

Put those together. For builders who ship, the tokens are nearly free. The cost now is your time and your nerve.

If you have a company, apply today. If you don't, spend the 5 hours this weekend and build something worth applying with.
virals.video_tip: 10-12s: price tag on a Claude card dropping to $0, then a 5-hour timer over a code editor, caption the tools are free, ship something.

virals.angle: Agents are getting their own internet
virals.inspired_by: @haakamaujla AgentID (437k) + @ky__zo One inbox (409k) + @shengkunye monid.ai (440k) + @ayanb Ampersand (785k) + @cursor_ai phone control (136k)
virals.draft_en:
Five launches in one day, all for agents, not people.

AgentID: sign in with Google, but for AI agents. One: an inbox where your agents ask you questions and you answer by voice. monid.ai: agents discover, run and pay for 2,500 APIs at runtime. Ampersand: agents act inside Salesforce and SAP. Cursor: run your desktop agents from your phone.

Last week the ask was memory and identity. This week people shipped it.

The next million users of your product may not have hands.

Pick one action in your app and make it usable by an agent: an API, an MCP tool, or agent sign-in.
virals.video_tip: 12s: a little agent avatar walking through doors labeled login, inbox, payments, Salesforce, caption agents are getting their own internet.

virals.angle: Every app is open source now
virals.inspired_by: @amasad AI decompilation (322k) + @signulll (75k) + @levelsio Quake III in a tweet (31k) + WASM ports (84k)
virals.draft_en:
Amjad Masad: AI-powered reverse engineering is getting so good that soon all software will be de facto open source.

signüll said it shorter: every piece of software minus the model weights is now effectively open source.

Meanwhile Pieter is porting classic games to the browser and just put Quake III, with multiplayer, inside a tweet.

If code can be read and rebuilt by anyone with an agent, code is not your moat.

Your moat is speed, distribution and the people who trust you.

Ask yourself: if a competitor cloned your app tonight, why would users stay? Post your answer.
virals.video_tip: 10s: compiled binary blob dissolving into readable source code, then a Quake match running in a tweet card, caption code is not the moat.

virals.angle: There is no secret agent setup
virals.inspired_by: @dhh setup (97k) + @ThePrimeagen terminal agents (117k) + @trq212 abstraction (260k) + @swyx default agent poll (17k) + @davidfowl monorepo (87k)
virals.draft_en:
People keep asking DHH for his agent setup. His answer: any harness, multiple agents at once, barely any skills, adversarial reviews. No magic sauce. The models are great out of the box.

ThePrimeagen admitted most of his work is now the terminal, an agent, and some review.

Thariq added the catch: working at a higher level still requires understanding the lower levels.

So the edge is not the tool list. It is review. Agents write, you judge.

This week, run two agents on the same task and have a third review both. Keep whichever survives.
virals.video_tip: 10s: two agent terminals writing side by side, a third one stamping red and green marks, caption no magic, just review.

virals.angle: Post what the model can't do
virals.draft_en:
"A.I. knows everything, yet understands nothing."

Neil deGrasse Tyson, 1.5M views.

Same day, Pieter's post-AGI thesis hit 743k: scarce coastal or mountain land with clean air. He already owns it and keeps buying.

Two of the biggest AI posts of the day were about what AI cannot do or cannot make.

People are tired of capability lists. They want to know where humans still win: understanding, taste, trust, a real place.

Post one task in your work where you still beat the model, and show the example side by side.
virals.video_tip: 10s: an encyclopedia flipping pages fast while a question mark hangs over it, then a coastline shot tagged scarce, caption what AI can't copy.

virals_narrative: Window Oct 6 through morning Oct 7 CT. Pieter again carries the watchlist: his post-AGI land thesis (743k★) and the Airbnb reviewgate response (348k★) lead, and he keeps shipping on top of the conversation with a Mistral Large 4 nod (126k★), a 0% AI tax pitch for the EU, WASM game ports and Quake III playable inside a tweet. Alex Finn's '5 hours of vibe coding' line (425k★) and two Hark posts push the AI-money and proactive-agent lanes, Tony Dinh's 'RIP Jev' (154k★) marks OpenAI's Decisions API, Greg lists 13 categories left to build, and Logan ships Nano Banana 2.1. Outsiders are dominated by agent infrastructure (AgentID, One inbox, monid.ai, Ampersand, Cursor on your phone), the Claude Startups expansion (3.67M★) with an indie founder's free-Claude-Code receipt, Figma's agent leaving beta, and a 'no magic setup' consensus from DHH and ThePrimeagen. Counterweight: Neil deGrasse Tyson's 'knows everything, understands nothing' (1.53M★) and the idea that AI decompilation makes all software open source.

Agents get their own stack: AgentID sign-in for agents (437k★), One agent inbox with voice (409k★), monid.ai tool marketplace for agents (440k★), Ampersand enterprise integrations (785k★), Cursor agents from your phone (136k★)
All software is open now: AI decompilation (Amjad 322k★), 'everything minus the weights is open source' (signüll 75k★), Pieter's Quake III inside a tweet (31k★) and WASM game ports (84k★)

No magic setup: DHH 'any harness, multiple agents, adversarial reviews' (97k★), ThePrimeagen working from the terminal via agent (117k★), Thariq on abstraction (260k★), swyx's default coding agent poll (17k★), monorepos for agents (87k★), Ben's local vs cloud question (10k★)
Open weights outside the US and China: Mistral Large 4 (Arthur Mensch 115k★, Pieter 126k★), Pieter's 0% AI tax for EU (49k★)

Agents with taste and initiative: Figma agent out of beta (1.26M★), Hark proactive agent (Alex 70k★ + 65k★), Nano Banana 2.1 price drop (Logan 86k★), Grok Bot routing to the best model per task (Alex 10k), Rowan's outfit app (6k)
What AI can't copy: Neil deGrasse Tyson 'knows everything, understands nothing' (1.53M★), Pieter's post-AGI land thesis (743k★)
Platform kills wrappers, receipts keep trust: OpenAI Decisions API 'RIP Jev' (Tony 154k★), Airbnb reviewgate continues (Pieter 348k★, 'Maybe it's working?' 95k★, government-owned hotels 58k★)
